messages:
ana: paging oncall - we just got an alert: 95th latency for text-generation route spiked from ~120ms to 2.4s across eu-west-1 and us-east-1 :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH latency observed on /v1/generate (route: redwood-text, model: rdx-13b-q8) - sustained >30m; impact: increased tail for small prompt customers.
nana: sorry typo, ana here. current traffic mix shows a sudden increase in long-context summarization requests that are getting batched together with short chat completions.
kevin: digging into scheduler metrics now. seeing continuous-batcher queue depth grow then KV cache miss rates spike -> paging.
jamal: kv-cache eviction rate jumped ~8x at 13:22 UTC, followed by pack-shed events. likely cache blowup from long-seq hot keys.
nana: which customers impacted? maria can you flag any support threads?
maria: support: two enterprise customers reported degraded UX (search latency) around 13:25. CS is aware, flagged severity 2.
kevin: root cause hypothesis: recent batch config change (auto_pack=true + max_batch_delay_ms=40) is causing long requests to keep inflight and fill KV working set, pushing smaller requests out -> scheduler unfairness.
jamal: reproducing locally with mixed workload (short=32 tokens, long=1024 tokens) shows small requests get starved when pack window hits 64k tokens per batch.
nana: mitigation plan? we need quick mitigation to restore short-request latency.
kevin: immediate options: 1) reduce max_batch_delay_ms to 5ms 2) add per-length bucketing so long/short don't mix 3) throttle long requests at ingress 4) fallback to smaller model variant for long seqs.
nana: do 1 + 3 now; 2 is a mid-term patch, 4 requires model rollout approval.
jamal: I'll push a hotfix to batch-config to set max_batch_delay_ms=5 and enable per-request inflight limit per bucket: `max_inflight_per_bucket: 8`.
ops-bot: deploy triggered by jamal: ci/cd pipeline: deploy/batch-config-hotfix -> canary (10%) -> prod.
kevin: canary metrics look good for 5 minutes. short-request p95 dropped back to ~140ms on canary nodes.
maria: CS: customers seeing partial improvement, one more ticket opened but UX improving.
nana: escalate to page team to roll to 100% and open an oncall handoff for regression postmortem. I'm assigning to kevin for incident lead.
kevin: rolling to 100% now. monitoring: KV eviction rate trending down, batch queue length stable.
jamal: while rolling, I'll back out the `auto_pack=true` change we made in the last deployment; that seems to exacerbate packing of long requests. diff in config: ```- auto_pack: true
+ auto_pack: false
```
kevin: win: tail latency restored to normal for short requests. but we still see throughput dip 5% for very long requests - acceptable tradeoff for customer-facing SLAs.
maria: note customers affected and timeline for postmortem: impacted 13:22-13:38 UTC, partial mitigation at 13:30, full roll at 13:36.
nana: please confirm no data loss and whether any retries exacerbated load.
jamal: logs show increased 429s for long requests during the surge; majority are client retries (exponential backoff honors), no persistent errors from runtime.
kevin: post-incident action items: - hotfix verification & rollback checklist - long-term: implement length-based batching + KV heap guards - observability: add alert for mixed-batch starvation (short_request_p95 > x while long_request_inflight > y) - add customer-facing incident message draft.
maria: I'll draft customer comms: short note explaining degradation and steps taken; ask CS for impacted customer list.
nana: oncall handoff to kevin for followups, jamal for runtime patching. I'm pausing paging, set severity to S2.
incident-bot: Incident S2 - root cause: continuous-batching config + KV cache blowup causing scheduler starvation for short requests. Remediation: reduced batch delay, disabled auto_pack, rolled config to 100%. Follow-ups assigned in tickets #INC-2219 and #ENG-RT-456.
kevin: creating playbook entry for similar regressions (pack thresholds, max_inflight tuning). Will add example commands and dashboards.
jamal: also adding a safety guard: if per-shard KV evictions > threshold, switch to strict bucketing mode automatically.
maria: CS will send an interim customer message in ~30m.
nana: thanks all. leaving notes in the incident doc and handing back to normal ops.
kevin: linking quick logs/commands we used:
```
# check batch queue depth
kubectl logs -f deploy/batcher --tail=200 | jq '.queue_len'

# patch to set delay
redwoodctl rollout set-config batcher --max_batch_delay_ms=5 --auto_pack=false
```
kevin: closing thread; moving to postmortem queue. final note: keep an eye on scheduled nightly jobs that may generate large summaries - they were the likely source of long request influx.
